templates.name: adminer
templates.title: Adminer
templates.description: A web page to browse and edit a database, behind a user name and password.
templates.notes: Adminer is at https://{{domain}}, behind Team only: its user name is team, and its password is shown once after Create. At its own login, give the address of a database this server can reach. A database app of the same project and environment answers by name: <app>-<service>, or just <app> when it is that app's only service with ports, and its installed notice shows the exact address (the PostgreSQL template installed as postgres is postgres-postgres, port 5432). That needs a Caravana whose installed notice lists addresses: on an older one a database inside another Caravana app is not reachable by name.

inputs.name: domain
inputs.label: Domain
inputs.help: Its DNS must point at this server.

templates.compose:
# Adminer (https://www.adminer.org): a web page to look into a database (PostgreSQL, MySQL,
# SQLite and others) that is reachable by address. It is behind Team only.
services:
  adminer:
    image: adminer:5.5.1
    expose: ["8080"]
    mem_limit: 256m

templates.name: codemagic-patch
templates.title: Codemagic Patch
templates.description: Over-the-air updates for React Native and Capacitor apps, signing in with GitHub, Bitbucket Cloud or GitLab, on R2 or Google Cloud buckets.
templates.notes: Before you install: Codemagic publishes no server image, so build one from the release tag into a private registry (Caravana's deploy/examples/codemagic-patch/RUNBOOK.md has a workflow for it) and add the registry's login in Settings, Registries. Make two buckets, one public and one private, and a key with read and write on both. On Google Cloud: the downloads URL is https://storage.googleapis.com/<public bucket>, give allUsers the role Storage Legacy Object Reader on it (read by name, no listing), and use a service account's HMAC key. On R2: give the public bucket a custom domain and use it as the downloads URL. Choose how people sign in and make an OAuth app at that provider. GitHub: an OAuth App whose homepage is https://{{domain}}. Bitbucket: Workspace settings, OAuth consumers, Add consumer, callback URL https://{{domain}}/auth/callback, This is a private consumer checked, permissions Account: Read and Email. GitLab: an application with the redirect URI https://{{domain}}/auth/callback and the scopes the dashboard asks for. Then sign in at https://{{domain}} with the admin email, which must be your confirmed primary email at the provider. Both addresses are written into your apps' builds, so choose them once. Postgres is backed up every day at 03:00 UTC, keeping 14.

inputs.name: image
inputs.label: Server image
inputs.help: The image you built, with its version tag (not latest).

inputs.name: domain
inputs.label: Server domain
inputs.help: The API and dashboard. DNS must point at this server. The sign-in callback is https://<domain>/auth/callback.

inputs.name: signin
inputs.label: Sign-in with
inputs.help: How people sign in to the dashboard. Each provider asks for its own OAuth app below.

inputs.name: gh_client_id
inputs.label: GitHub OAuth client ID
inputs.help: From the GitHub OAuth app the dashboard signs in with.

inputs.name: gh_client_secret
inputs.label: GitHub OAuth client secret
inputs.help: From the same GitHub OAuth app.

inputs.name: bb_client_id
inputs.label: Bitbucket consumer key
inputs.help: The Key of the Bitbucket OAuth consumer. Its callback URL is https://<domain>/auth/callback.

inputs.name: bb_client_secret
inputs.label: Bitbucket consumer secret
inputs.help: The Secret of the same OAuth consumer.

inputs.name: gl_client_id
inputs.label: GitLab application ID
inputs.help: From the GitLab application. Its redirect URI is https://<domain>/auth/callback.

inputs.name: gl_client_secret
inputs.label: GitLab application secret
inputs.help: The Secret of the same GitLab application.

inputs.name: gl_base_url
inputs.label: GitLab address
inputs.help: Only for a GitLab you host yourself. Empty means https://gitlab.com.

inputs.name: admin_email
inputs.label: Admin email
inputs.help: The first admin of the dashboard.

inputs.name: public_url
inputs.label: Downloads URL
inputs.help: Where apps download updates: the public bucket's address. https://storage.googleapis.com/<bucket> on Google Cloud, or the R2 bucket's custom domain.

inputs.name: bucket
inputs.label: Public bucket
inputs.help: The public bucket: anyone may read its files.

inputs.name: internal_bucket
inputs.label: Private bucket
inputs.help: The bucket for the server's own files. It must never be public.

inputs.name: s3_endpoint
inputs.label: S3 endpoint
inputs.help: The buckets' S3 API: https://storage.googleapis.com on Google Cloud, https://<account ID>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com on R2.

inputs.name: s3_region
inputs.label: S3 region
inputs.help: auto on R2; the buckets' location on Google Cloud, such as us-central1.

inputs.name: s3_access_key_id
inputs.label: S3 access key ID
inputs.help: With read and write on both buckets: an R2 API token, or a Google Cloud HMAC key of a service account.

inputs.name: s3_secret_access_key
inputs.label: S3 secret access key
inputs.help: From the same token or HMAC key.

templates.compose:
# Codemagic Patch (https://patch.codemagic.io/docs/): over-the-air updates for React Native and
# Capacitor apps. It is the upstream self-host stack without Caddy and Silo: Traefik serves the
# API and dashboard, and apps download updates from two S3-compatible buckets (Cloudflare R2 or
# Google Cloud Storage: one public, one private for the server's own files). Two services: the
# Patch server, and Postgres on a volume. Sign-in is through GitHub, Bitbucket Cloud or GitLab: only the chosen one's lines are kept. Upstream publishes no
# server image: build yours and give its address (the notes say how). No secret is in this file.
services:
  server:
    image: "{{image}}"
    expose: ["3000"]
    mem_reservation: 512m
    mem_limit: 1024m
    environment:
      MODE: all # API and release worker in one process
      HOST: 0.0.0.0
      PORT: "3000"
      RUN_MIGRATIONS: "true"
      LOGGER: "true"
      SERVER_URL: "https://{{domain}}"
      PUBLIC_BASE_URL: "{{public_url}}"
      STORAGE_ADAPTER: s3
      S3_BUCKET: "{{bucket}}"
      S3_INTERNAL_BUCKET: "{{internal_bucket}}"
      S3_REGION: "{{s3_region}}"
      S3_ENDPOINT: "{{s3_endpoint}}"
      S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE: "true"
      DELIVERY_ADAPTER: base-url
      GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID: "{{gh_client_id}}" # when signin=github
      BITBUCKET_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID: "{{bb_client_id}}" # when signin=bitbucket
      BITBUCKET_OAUTH_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_URIS: "https://{{domain}}/auth/callback" # when signin=bitbucket
      GITLAB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID: "{{gl_client_id}}" # when signin=gitlab
      GITLAB_OAUTH_BASE_URL: "{{gl_base_url}}" # when gl_base_url
      INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAILS: "{{admin_email}}"
      REGISTRATION_MODE: invite_only
      SERVER_TELEMETRY: "false"
      SERVER_UPDATE_CHECK: "true"

  postgres:
    image: postgres:16
    expose: ["5432"]
    mem_limit: 512m
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: patch
      POSTGRES_DB: patch
    volumes:
      - db:/var/lib/postgresql/data

volumes:
  db: {}

templates.name: continuwuity
templates.title: Continuwuity
templates.description: A Matrix homeserver in one container, with its own database: your own chat server that federates with every other Matrix server.
templates.notes: Your Matrix IDs end in :{{server_name}}, for good: that name can't change later. The server answers at https://{{domain}}. If {{server_name}} isn't {{domain}}, the site at https://{{server_name}} must serve two files so other servers and apps find this one: /.well-known/matrix/server with {"m.server": "{{domain}}:443"}, and /.well-known/matrix/client with {"m.homeserver": {"base_url": "https://{{domain}}"}}, both as application/json, the client one also with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. First account: on its first start the server writes a one-time registration token to its log; open the app's Logs, find the line that says "using the registration token", then register in a Matrix client (Element, Cinny) against https://{{domain}} with that token. Nobody else can sign up: more accounts are made from the admin room. Check federation at https://federationtester.matrix.org with {{server_name}}. Everything it keeps is on one volume, which Caravana backs up every day at 03:00 UTC (the server stops for a few seconds). Voice and video calls aren't set up: they need a TURN server.

inputs.name: domain
inputs.label: Domain
inputs.help: Where the server answers. Its DNS must point at this server.

inputs.name: server_name
inputs.label: Server name
inputs.help: The part after the colon in your Matrix IDs (@you:example.com). Usually your bare domain. It can never change.

templates.compose:
# Continuwuity (https://continuwuity.org): a Matrix homeserver in one container, with an embedded
# RocksDB database, so no Postgres. Everything it keeps is in /var/lib/continuwuity, on the volume.
# The image's own command starts the server. Federation and clients both reach it over HTTPS on 443
# through Caravana's Traefik (Matrix's .well-known delegation, see the notes), so port 8448 isn't needed.
# Traefik passes Matrix's encoded paths (%2F, %23) as they are: allowed by default since Traefik v3.6.7.
services:
  continuwuity:
    image: ghcr.io/continuwuity/continuwuity:v26.9.4
    expose: ["8008"]
    # Joining large public rooms makes memory and CPU spike for a while.
    mem_reservation: 512m
    mem_limit: 2048m
    environment:
      # Permanent: it is the part after the colon in every user ID (@you:server_name). Changing it
      # later means a new, empty server.
      CONTINUWUITY_SERVER_NAME: "{{server_name}}"
      CONTINUWUITY_DATABASE_PATH: /var/lib/continuwuity
      CONTINUWUITY_ADDRESS: 0.0.0.0
      CONTINUWUITY_PORT: "8008"
      # Where it fetches other servers' signing keys when it can't reach them directly.
      CONTINUWUITY_TRUSTED_SERVERS: '["matrix.org"]'
      # Sign-ups stay closed: the first account uses the one-time token the server prints at its first
      # start, and later accounts are made from the admin room.
      CONTINUWUITY_ALLOW_REGISTRATION: "false"
    volumes:
      - continuwuity-data:/var/lib/continuwuity

volumes:
  continuwuity-data: {}

templates.name: frunchy
templates.title: Frunchy
templates.description: Your anime identity in numbers: Frunchy turns your Crunchyroll watch history into statistics you can share.
templates.notes: Frunchy signs people in through Umbral, so install Umbral first (its own template), claim it, and in Umbral's admin create a web application with the redirect URI https://{{domain}}/signin-umbral: its client ID and secret are what you typed here. First account: on its first start Frunchy writes a one-time setup invite to its log; open the app's Logs, find the line "Invite", then sign in at https://{{domain}}/signin with Umbral and paste it. That account is an operator; to make it the root operator (who can open sign-ups), set Frunchy__RootOperator to its username on the Variables page. Sign-up is by invite until then. For studios, genres and seasons, add Frunchy__Mal__ClientId (a client ID from myanimelist.net/apiconfig) on the Variables page. Then install the Frunchy browser extension and connect it with the sync key from your account page. Postgres is backed up every day at 03:00 UTC, keeping 14. The data-protection key Caravana made is kept as a secret: losing it only signs everyone out.

inputs.name: domain
inputs.label: Domain
inputs.help: Its DNS must point at this server. Your profile pages live here.

inputs.name: umbral_domain
inputs.label: Umbral's domain
inputs.help: The Umbral that signs people in (install it from its template first).

inputs.name: umbral_client_id
inputs.label: Umbral client ID
inputs.help: From the web application you created in Umbral's admin.

inputs.name: umbral_client_secret
inputs.label: Umbral client secret
inputs.help: Shown once when you created the application in Umbral.

templates.compose:
# Frunchy (https://github.com/jjchiw/frunchy): your anime watch history in numbers, from a browser
# extension's sync of your Crunchyroll history. Two services: Frunchy, and Postgres 18 on a volume. Every
# secret (the database password, the data-protection key, the sign-in client's secret) is in the services'
# secrets (see template.json); no secret is in this file. Without federation (Megafono): a plain web app.
# 10.99.0.1 is Traefik's address on a Caravana host: Frunchy believes X-Forwarded-* from it only.
services:
  frunchy:
    image: ghcr.io/jjchiw/frunchy:0.10.0
    expose: ["8080"]
    mem_reservation: 256m
    mem_limit: 768m
    environment:
      Frunchy__TrustedProxies: 10.99.0.1
      # Sign-in through Umbral, the only provider this template sets up (Frunchy keeps no passwords).
      Frunchy__Auth__Providers__Umbral__Enabled: "true"
      Frunchy__Auth__Providers__Umbral__Authority: "https://{{umbral_domain}}"
      Frunchy__Auth__Providers__Umbral__ClientId: "{{umbral_client_id}}"
      # MyAnimeList enrichment (studios, genres, seasons) is off until Frunchy__Mal__ClientId is set
      # on the app's Variables page (the template's notes say so).
    # No depends_on: services start together, and Frunchy waits up to 60 s for Postgres by itself
    # (Frunchy:Database:StartupWaitSeconds); Nomad restarts it if Postgres takes longer.

  postgres:
    image: postgres:18-alpine
    expose: ["5432"]
    mem_reservation: 256m
    mem_limit: 512m
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: frunchydb
      POSTGRES_USER: frunchy
    volumes:
      - frunchy-pg:/var/lib/postgresql # Postgres 18's layout: the data is in a versioned folder under here

volumes:
  frunchy-pg: {}

templates.name: hollo
templates.title: Hollo
templates.description: A single-user fediverse server: your own account on Mastodon's network.
templates.notes: Open https://{{domain}}/setup first, to create your account (the first visit is the owner's). Your handle will be @you@{{domain}}; it can't change after you federate. Hollo may restart once or twice while Postgres starts: that is normal. Postgres is backed up every day at 03:00 UTC, keeping 14.

inputs.name: domain
inputs.label: Domain
inputs.help: Its DNS must point at this server. It becomes part of your handle.

templates.compose:
# Hollo (https://docs.hollo.social): a single-user fediverse server. Two services: Hollo, with its
# media on a volume (DRIVE_DISK=fs), and Postgres on a volume. The database password is shared by
# both through the services' secrets (see template.json); no secret is in this file.
services:
  hollo:
    image: ghcr.io/fedify-dev/hollo:0.9.25
    expose: ["3000"]
    mem_limit: 768m
    environment:
      BEHIND_PROXY: "true" # Traefik terminates HTTPS in front of it
      LOG_LEVEL: info
      DRIVE_DISK: fs
      FS_STORAGE_PATH: /var/lib/hollo
      STORAGE_URL_BASE: "https://{{domain}}/assets"
    volumes:
      - media:/var/lib/hollo

  postgres:
    image: postgres:17
    expose: ["5432"]
    mem_limit: 512m
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: hollo
      POSTGRES_DB: hollo
    volumes:
      - db:/var/lib/postgresql/data

volumes:
  media: {}
  db: {}

templates.name: peertube
templates.title: PeerTube
templates.description: Video hosting on your own domain, federated with the fediverse, with the videos in an S3-compatible bucket (R2).
templates.notes: https://{{domain}} is permanent: every video and account address is tied to it. Buckets: {{bucket}} must be public at {{files_url}} (on R2, a custom domain or r2.dev) with a CORS rule that allows GET and HEAD from https://{{domain}}, or the player can't load videos; {{private_bucket}} must never be public. First sign-in: at its first start PeerTube makes the account root and writes its password once to its log. Open the app's Logs, search for "User password", sign in at https://{{domain}}/login as root, and change the password in My account, Settings. Sign-ups are closed and no email is set up: to send email, add PEERTUBE_SMTP_HOSTNAME, PEERTUBE_SMTP_PORT and PEERTUBE_SMTP_USERNAME to the peertube service's environment (Configure, Compose) and PEERTUBE_SMTP_PASSWORD as its secret, then open sign-ups in Administration if you want them. Transcoding uses up to 3 GB of memory; on a small server, move it to a remote runner on another machine (Administration, Remote runners). Backups: Postgres and PeerTube's volumes (thumbnails, avatars, plugins, settings) every day at 03:00 UTC, keeping 14; PeerTube stops for a few seconds during its backup. The videos are in the bucket, which Caravana doesn't back up. Redis holds only the job queue. Live streaming isn't set up: it needs the RTMP port, which a later version of this template adds.

inputs.name: domain
inputs.label: Domain
inputs.help: Where PeerTube answers. Its DNS must point at this server. It can never change.

inputs.name: admin_email
inputs.label: Admin email
inputs.help: The email of the root account.

inputs.name: s3_endpoint
inputs.label: S3 endpoint
inputs.help: Your bucket provider's S3 address. On R2: https://<account ID>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com

inputs.name: s3_region
inputs.label: S3 region
inputs.help: auto on R2.

inputs.name: bucket
inputs.label: Videos bucket
inputs.help: The public bucket for the videos, playlists and captions.

inputs.name: files_url
inputs.label: Videos bucket's public URL
inputs.help: Where browsers read that bucket: its R2 custom domain or r2.dev address.

inputs.name: private_bucket
inputs.label: Private bucket
inputs.help: For users' exports and kept original files. It must never be public.

inputs.name: s3_access_key_id
inputs.label: S3 access key ID
inputs.help: From an R2 API token with Object Read & Write on both buckets.

inputs.name: s3_secret_access_key
inputs.label: S3 secret access key
inputs.help: From the same API token.

templates.compose:
# PeerTube (https://joinpeertube.org): video hosting that federates with the fediverse. Three services:
# PeerTube, Postgres and Redis. Videos go to S3-compatible object storage (Cloudflare R2, or any other),
# so PeerTube's data volume keeps only thumbnails, avatars, captions' sources, plugins, logs and
# transcoding's temporary files. PeerTube's own Compose file also has nginx, certbot and postfix: here
# Caravana's Traefik serves HTTPS, and email is added after install (see the notes). Live streaming
# (RTMP on port 1935) isn't set up. No secret is in this file: they are the services' secrets (template.json).
services:
  peertube:
    image: chocobozzz/peertube:v8.3.2-trixie
    expose: ["9000"]
    # PeerTube itself needs about 500 MB; transcoding (ffmpeg) takes much more while it runs.
    mem_reservation: 768m
    mem_limit: 3072m
    environment:
      # Permanent: every video's and account's address (and federation) is tied to it.
      PEERTUBE_WEBSERVER_HOSTNAME: "{{domain}}"
      PEERTUBE_WEBSERVER_PORT: "443"
      PEERTUBE_WEBSERVER_HTTPS: "true"
      # Traefik reaches the copy from the private network: trust its X-Forwarded-For.
      PEERTUBE_TRUST_PROXY: '["loopback", "linklocal", "uniquelocal"]'
      PEERTUBE_DB_HOSTNAME: postgres
      PEERTUBE_DB_PORT: "5432"
      PEERTUBE_DB_NAME: peertube
      PEERTUBE_DB_USERNAME: peertube
      PEERTUBE_DB_SSL: "false"
      PEERTUBE_REDIS_HOSTNAME: redis
      PEERTUBE_REDIS_PORT: "6379"
      # The root account's email.
      PEERTUBE_ADMIN_EMAIL: "{{admin_email}}"
      PEERTUBE_SMTP_FROM: "noreply@{{domain}}"
      # Closed until email is set up (sign-ups need it to verify addresses).
      PEERTUBE_SIGNUP_ENABLED: "false"
      # Object storage. Path-style requests work with R2, MinIO and most others; the public URL replaces
      # the endpoint and bucket in every video address. The image sets no ACL (R2 has none): the public
      # bucket is public as a whole, and private videos are served through PeerTube.
      PEERTUBE_OBJECT_STORAGE_ENABLED: "true"
      PEERTUBE_OBJECT_STORAGE_ENDPOINT: "{{s3_endpoint}}"
      PEERTUBE_OBJECT_STORAGE_REGION: "{{s3_region}}"
      PEERTUBE_OBJECT_STORAGE_FORCE_PATH_STYLE: "true"
      PEERTUBE_OBJECT_STORAGE_STREAMING_PLAYLISTS_BUCKET_NAME: "{{bucket}}"
      PEERTUBE_OBJECT_STORAGE_STREAMING_PLAYLISTS_PREFIX: streaming-playlists/
      PEERTUBE_OBJECT_STORAGE_STREAMING_PLAYLISTS_BASE_URL: "{{files_url}}"
      PEERTUBE_OBJECT_STORAGE_WEB_VIDEOS_BUCKET_NAME: "{{bucket}}"
      PEERTUBE_OBJECT_STORAGE_WEB_VIDEOS_PREFIX: web-videos/
      PEERTUBE_OBJECT_STORAGE_WEB_VIDEOS_BASE_URL: "{{files_url}}"
      PEERTUBE_OBJECT_STORAGE_CAPTIONS_BUCKET_NAME: "{{bucket}}"
      PEERTUBE_OBJECT_STORAGE_CAPTIONS_PREFIX: captions/
      PEERTUBE_OBJECT_STORAGE_CAPTIONS_BASE_URL: "{{files_url}}"
      # Never public: users' exports, and the original files when the admin chooses to keep them.
      PEERTUBE_OBJECT_STORAGE_USER_EXPORTS_BUCKET_NAME: "{{private_bucket}}"
      PEERTUBE_OBJECT_STORAGE_USER_EXPORTS_PREFIX: user-exports/
      PEERTUBE_OBJECT_STORAGE_ORIGINAL_VIDEO_FILES_BUCKET_NAME: "{{private_bucket}}"
      PEERTUBE_OBJECT_STORAGE_ORIGINAL_VIDEO_FILES_PREFIX: original-video-files/
    volumes:
      - peertube-data:/data
      # Holds local-production.json: what the admin changes in Administration, Configuration.
      - peertube-config:/config

  postgres:
    # The major PeerTube's own Compose file names. Moving to a later major needs a dump and restore.
    image: postgres:17-alpine
    expose: ["5432"]
    mem_limit: 1024m
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: peertube
      POSTGRES_DB: peertube
    volumes:
      - db:/var/lib/postgresql/data

  redis:
    # Job queue (transcoding, federation) and caches. Its snapshot on the volume keeps queued jobs across
    # a restart; it isn't backed up.
    image: redis:8-alpine
    expose: ["6379"]
    mem_reservation: 128m
    mem_limit: 512m
    volumes:
      - redis-data:/data

volumes:
  peertube-data: {}
  peertube-config: {}
  db: {}
  redis-data: {}

templates.name: postgres
templates.title: PostgreSQL
templates.description: A PostgreSQL 17 database on a volume, backed up daily, with Adminer to look into it.
templates.notes: Adminer is at https://{{domain}}, behind Team only: its user name is team, and its password is shown once after Create. To log into the database from Adminer choose System PostgreSQL, Server postgres, Username app, Database app, and the password you typed. Other apps of this project and environment reach the database at <app name>-postgres:5432, so postgres-postgres:5432 if you keep the app name postgres (Adminer has a port too, so the bare app name isn't claimed), with Username app and Database app; the installed notice shows the exact address. That needs a Caravana whose installed notice lists addresses: on an older one other apps can't reach it by name, so add your own services to this app's Compose file (Configure, Compose), where they reach it at postgres:5432. Backups run every day at 03:00 UTC.

inputs.name: domain
inputs.label: Adminer domain
inputs.help: Where Adminer is served. Its DNS must point at this server.

inputs.name: db_password
inputs.label: Database password
inputs.help: The password of the app user. Keep a note of it: Caravana never shows it again.

templates.compose:
# A PostgreSQL database with Adminer, a web page to look into it. Postgres has no domain: other
# services of this app reach it as "postgres:5432". Adminer is the only public address, and it
# is behind Team only (a user name and password Caravana makes). The password of the database is
# typed at install, so its owner knows it; it isn't in this file.
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:17
    expose: ["5432"]
    mem_limit: 512m
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: app
      POSTGRES_DB: app
    volumes:
      - data:/var/lib/postgresql/data

  adminer:
    image: adminer:5.5.1
    expose: ["8080"]
    mem_limit: 256m
    environment:
      ADMINER_DEFAULT_SERVER: postgres

volumes:
  data: {}

templates.name: umbral
templates.title: Umbral
templates.description: An OpenID Connect provider that signs people in with social accounts or passkeys, no passwords.
templates.notes: The domain is part of every callback address you register with a sign-in provider, so choose it once. On its first start Umbral writes a one-time claim code to its log (look for the box that says "not configured yet"): open the app's Logs, then https://{{domain}} and claim the instance. Everything it keeps is on one volume, which Caravana backs up every day at 03:00 UTC (the volume is the key ring: without it every secret is lost).

inputs.name: domain
inputs.label: Domain
inputs.help: Its DNS must point at this server. It must be the exact address people use.

templates.compose:
# Umbral (https://github.com/Cosmic-Chimps/umbral): a self-hosted OpenID Connect provider that
# signs people in without passwords. One container with an embedded SQLite database. Everything it
# keeps (the database, signing keys, the Data Protection key ring) is in /data, on the volume.
# 10.99.0.1 is Traefik's address on a Caravana host: Umbral believes X-Forwarded-* from it only.
services:
  umbral:
    image: ghcr.io/cosmic-chimps/umbral:0.13.0
    expose: ["8080"]
    environment:
      UMBRAL__PUBLIC_ORIGIN: "https://{{domain}}"
      UMBRAL__TRUSTED_PROXIES: 10.99.0.1
    volumes:
      - umbral-data:/data

volumes:
  umbral-data: {}

templates.name: uptime-kuma
templates.title: Uptime Kuma
templates.description: A status monitor: watch your sites and services, and publish a status page.
templates.notes: Open https://{{domain}} and create the admin account: the first visitor becomes the admin, so do it now. Everything it keeps is on one volume, which Caravana backs up every day at 03:00 UTC.

inputs.name: domain
inputs.label: Domain
inputs.help: Its DNS must point at this server.

templates.compose:
# Uptime Kuma (https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma): a self-hosted status monitor and status
# page. One service; everything it keeps (its SQLite database, settings, monitor history) is in
# /app/data, on the volume. UPTIME_KUMA_DB_TYPE=sqlite skips the first-run database question.
services:
  uptime-kuma:
    image: louislam/uptime-kuma:2.5.11
    expose: ["3001"]
    mem_limit: 768m
    environment:
      UPTIME_KUMA_DB_TYPE: sqlite
    volumes:
      - data:/app/data

volumes:
  data: {}

templates.name: wazuh
templates.title: Wazuh
templates.description: A security platform: agents on your machines send events, Wazuh finds threats and shows them on a dashboard.
templates.notes: Open https://{{domain}} and sign in as admin with the password you typed. Wazuh needs about 4 GB of memory for its three services. Agents connect to the manager on ports 1514 (events) and 1515 (enrollment): they are published on this server's address, so open them in your cloud provider's firewall, and point each agent at this server's IP or a DNS name for it (not the dashboard's domain, which goes through the HTTPS proxy). The indexer is OpenSearch: every Caravana server already has vm.max_map_count at 262144 or more, which it needs. Backups run every day at 03:00 UTC: the indexer takes an OpenSearch snapshot of its indices while it runs, and the manager's volumes are archived, which stops the manager for a moment (agents reconnect on their own). A snapshot needs free disk about the size of the indices while it is uploaded. The certificates are made at install and are valid for ten years; the certificate authority's key isn't kept, so they can't be reissued without installing the app again.

inputs.name: domain
inputs.label: Dashboard domain
inputs.help: Its DNS must point at this server.

inputs.name: admin_password
inputs.label: Admin password
inputs.help: The password of the dashboard's admin user (also the manager's indexer login). Keep a note of it: Caravana never shows it again.

secrets.name: WAZUH_YML
secrets.value:
hosts:
  - default:
      url: "https://manager"
      port: 55000
      username: wazuh-wui
      password: "{{api_password}}.Wz1"
      run_as: true

secrets.name: INTERNAL_USERS
secrets.value:
---
# The indexer's internal users: only the two Wazuh needs, with passwords made at install.
# Wazuh's demo users (kibanaro, logstash, readall, snapshotrestore) are left out on purpose.
_meta:
  type: "internalusers"
  config_version: 2

admin:
  hash: "{{admin_password|bcrypt}}"
  reserved: true
  backend_roles:
  - "admin"
  description: "Admin user"

kibanaserver:
  hash: "{{dashboard_password|bcrypt}}"
  reserved: true
  description: "The dashboard's user"

templates.compose:
# Wazuh (https://github.com/wazuh/wazuh-docker, single-node 4.14.11): a security platform. Three
# services: the indexer (OpenSearch, where alerts are kept), the manager (agents connect to it on
# 1514 and 1515) and the dashboard. The certificates and every password are made at install; the
# private keys and the files that hold passwords are secret files (in the overlay), never here.
# Service names are DNS labels, so wazuh.indexer is "indexer" in every config below.
services:
  indexer:
    image: wazuh/wazuh-indexer:4.14.11
    expose: ["9200"]
    mem_reservation: 1536m
    mem_limit: 2g
    environment:
      OPENSEARCH_JAVA_OPTS: "-Xms1g -Xmx1g"
    ulimits:
      memlock:
        soft: -1
        hard: -1
      nofile:
        soft: 65536
        hard: 65536
    volumes:
      - indexer-data:/var/lib/wazuh-indexer
      - indexer-snapshots:/var/lib/wazuh-indexer-snapshots
    configs:
      - source: indexer
        target: /usr/share/wazuh-indexer/config/opensearch.yml

  manager:
    image: wazuh/wazuh-manager:4.14.11
    expose: ["1514", "1515", "55000"]
    mem_reservation: 1024m
    mem_limit: 1536m
    environment:
      INDEXER_URL: https://indexer:9200
      INDEXER_USERNAME: admin
      FILEBEAT_SSL_VERIFICATION_MODE: full
      SSL_CERTIFICATE_AUTHORITIES: /etc/ssl/root-ca.pem
      SSL_CERTIFICATE: /etc/ssl/filebeat.pem
      SSL_KEY: /etc/ssl/filebeat.key
      API_USERNAME: wazuh-wui
    ulimits:
      memlock:
        soft: -1
        hard: -1
      nofile:
        soft: 655360
        hard: 655360
    volumes:
      - manager-api-configuration:/var/ossec/api/configuration
      - manager-etc:/var/ossec/etc
      - manager-logs:/var/ossec/logs
      - manager-queue:/var/ossec/queue
      - manager-var-multigroups:/var/ossec/var/multigroups
      - manager-integrations:/var/ossec/integrations
      - manager-active-response:/var/ossec/active-response/bin
      - manager-agentless:/var/ossec/agentless
      - manager-wodles:/var/ossec/wodles
      - manager-filebeat-etc:/etc/filebeat
      - manager-filebeat-var:/var/lib/filebeat
    configs:
      - source: manager
        target: /wazuh-config-mount/etc/ossec.conf

  dashboard:
    image: wazuh/wazuh-dashboard:4.14.11
    expose: ["5601"]
    mem_reservation: 768m
    mem_limit: 1g
    environment:
      INDEXER_USERNAME: admin
      WAZUH_API_URL: https://manager
      DASHBOARD_USERNAME: kibanaserver
      API_USERNAME: wazuh-wui
    volumes:
      - dashboard-config:/usr/share/wazuh-dashboard/data/wazuh/config
      - dashboard-custom:/usr/share/wazuh-dashboard/plugins/wazuh/public/assets/custom
    configs:
      - source: dashboard
        target: /usr/share/wazuh-dashboard/config/opensearch_dashboards.yml

configs:
  indexer:
    content: |
      network.host: "0.0.0.0"
      node.name: "indexer"
      cluster.name: "wazuh-cluster"
      path.data: /var/lib/wazuh-indexer
      path.logs: /var/log/wazuh-indexer
      path.repo: /var/lib/wazuh-indexer-snapshots
      discovery.type: single-node
      compatibility.override_main_response_version: true
      plugins.security.ssl.http.pemcert_filepath: /usr/share/wazuh-indexer/config/certs/wazuh.indexer.pem
      plugins.security.ssl.http.pemkey_filepath: /usr/share/wazuh-indexer/config/certs/wazuh.indexer.key
      plugins.security.ssl.http.pemtrustedcas_filepath: /usr/share/wazuh-indexer/config/certs/root-ca.pem
      plugins.security.ssl.transport.pemcert_filepath: /usr/share/wazuh-indexer/config/certs/wazuh.indexer.pem
      plugins.security.ssl.transport.pemkey_filepath: /usr/share/wazuh-indexer/config/certs/wazuh.indexer.key
      plugins.security.ssl.transport.pemtrustedcas_filepath: /usr/share/wazuh-indexer/config/certs/root-ca.pem
      plugins.security.ssl.http.enabled: true
      plugins.security.ssl.transport.enforce_hostname_verification: false
      plugins.security.ssl.transport.resolve_hostname: false
      plugins.security.ssl.http.enabled_ciphers:
        - "TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256"
        - "TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384"
        - "TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256"
        - "TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384"
      plugins.security.ssl.http.enabled_protocols:
        - "TLSv1.2"
      plugins.security.authcz.admin_dn:
      - "CN=admin,OU=Wazuh,O=Wazuh,L=California,C=US"
      plugins.security.check_snapshot_restore_write_privileges: true
      plugins.security.enable_snapshot_restore_privilege: true
      plugins.security.nodes_dn:
      - "CN=indexer,OU=Wazuh,O=Wazuh,L=California,C=US"
      plugins.security.restapi.roles_enabled:
      - "all_access"
      - "security_rest_api_access"
      plugins.security.system_indices.enabled: true
      plugins.security.system_indices.indices: [".opendistro-alerting-config", ".opendistro-alerting-alert*", ".opendistro-anomaly-results*", ".opendistro-anomaly-detector*", ".opendistro-anomaly-checkpoints", ".opendistro-anomaly-detection-state", ".opendistro-reports-*", ".opendistro-notifications-*", ".opendistro-notebooks", ".opensearch-observability", ".opendistro-asynchronous-search-response*", ".replication-metadata-store"]
      plugins.security.allow_default_init_securityindex: true
      cluster.routing.allocation.disk.threshold_enabled: false
  manager:
    content: |
      <ossec_config>
        <global>
          <jsonout_output>yes</jsonout_output>
          <alerts_log>yes</alerts_log>
          <logall>no</logall>
          <logall_json>no</logall_json>
          <email_notification>no</email_notification>
          <smtp_server>smtp.example.wazuh.com</smtp_server>
          <email_from>wazuh@example.wazuh.com</email_from>
          <email_to>recipient@example.wazuh.com</email_to>
          <email_maxperhour>12</email_maxperhour>
          <email_log_source>alerts.log</email_log_source>
          <agents_disconnection_time>10m</agents_disconnection_time>
          <agents_disconnection_alert_time>0</agents_disconnection_alert_time>
        </global>

        <alerts>
          <log_alert_level>3</log_alert_level>
          <email_alert_level>12</email_alert_level>
        </alerts>

        <!-- Choose between "plain", "json", or "plain,json" for the format of internal logs -->
        <logging>
          <log_format>plain</log_format>
        </logging>

        <remote>
          <connection>secure</connection>
          <port>1514</port>
          <protocol>tcp</protocol>
          <queue_size>131072</queue_size>
        </remote>

        <!-- Policy monitoring -->
        <rootcheck>
          <disabled>no</disabled>
          <check_files>yes</check_files>
          <check_trojans>yes</check_trojans>
          <check_dev>yes</check_dev>
          <check_sys>yes</check_sys>
          <check_pids>yes</check_pids>
          <check_ports>yes</check_ports>
          <check_if>yes</check_if>

          <!-- Frequency that rootcheck is executed - every 12 hours -->
          <frequency>43200</frequency>

          <rootkit_files>etc/rootcheck/rootkit_files.txt</rootkit_files>
          <rootkit_trojans>etc/rootcheck/rootkit_trojans.txt</rootkit_trojans>

          <skip_nfs>yes</skip_nfs>
        </rootcheck>

        <wodle name="cis-cat">
          <disabled>yes</disabled>
          <timeout>1800</timeout>
          <interval>1d</interval>
          <scan-on-start>yes</scan-on-start>

          <java_path>wodles/java</java_path>
          <ciscat_path>wodles/ciscat</ciscat_path>
        </wodle>

        <!-- Osquery integration -->
        <wodle name="osquery">
          <disabled>yes</disabled>
          <run_daemon>yes</run_daemon>
          <log_path>/var/log/osquery/osqueryd.results.log</log_path>
          <config_path>/etc/osquery/osquery.conf</config_path>
          <add_labels>yes</add_labels>
        </wodle>

        <!-- System inventory -->
        <wodle name="syscollector">
          <disabled>no</disabled>
          <interval>1h</interval>
          <scan_on_start>yes</scan_on_start>
          <hardware>yes</hardware>
          <os>yes</os>
          <network>yes</network>
          <packages>yes</packages>
          <ports all="yes">yes</ports>
          <processes>yes</processes>

          <!-- Database synchronization settings -->
          <synchronization>
            <max_eps>10</max_eps>
          </synchronization>
        </wodle>

        <sca>
          <enabled>yes</enabled>
          <scan_on_start>yes</scan_on_start>
          <interval>12h</interval>
          <skip_nfs>yes</skip_nfs>
        </sca>

        <vulnerability-detection>
          <enabled>yes</enabled>
          <index-status>yes</index-status>
          <feed-update-interval>60m</feed-update-interval>
        </vulnerability-detection>

        <indexer>
          <enabled>yes</enabled>
          <hosts>
            <host>https://indexer:9200</host>
          </hosts>
          <ssl>
            <certificate_authorities>
              <ca>/etc/ssl/root-ca.pem</ca>
            </certificate_authorities>
            <certificate>/etc/ssl/filebeat.pem</certificate>
            <key>/etc/ssl/filebeat.key</key>
          </ssl>
        </indexer>

        <!-- File integrity monitoring -->
        <syscheck>
          <disabled>no</disabled>

          <!-- Frequency that syscheck is executed default every 12 hours -->
          <frequency>43200</frequency>

          <scan_on_start>yes</scan_on_start>

          <!-- Generate alert when new file detected -->
          <alert_new_files>yes</alert_new_files>

          <!-- Don't ignore files that change more than 'frequency' times -->
          <auto_ignore frequency="10" timeframe="3600">no</auto_ignore>

          <!-- Directories to check  (perform all possible verifications) -->
          <directories>/etc,/usr/bin,/usr/sbin</directories>
          <directories>/bin,/sbin,/boot</directories>

          <!-- Files/directories to ignore -->
          <ignore>/etc/mtab</ignore>
          <ignore>/etc/hosts.deny</ignore>
          <ignore>/etc/mail/statistics</ignore>
          <ignore>/etc/random-seed</ignore>
          <ignore>/etc/random.seed</ignore>
          <ignore>/etc/adjtime</ignore>
          <ignore>/etc/httpd/logs</ignore>
          <ignore>/etc/utmpx</ignore>
          <ignore>/etc/wtmpx</ignore>
          <ignore>/etc/cups/certs</ignore>
          <ignore>/etc/dumpdates</ignore>
          <ignore>/etc/svc/volatile</ignore>

          <!-- File types to ignore -->
          <ignore type="sregex">.log$|.swp$</ignore>

          <!-- Check the file, but never compute the diff -->
          <nodiff>/etc/ssl/private.key</nodiff>

          <skip_nfs>yes</skip_nfs>
          <skip_dev>yes</skip_dev>
          <skip_proc>yes</skip_proc>
          <skip_sys>yes</skip_sys>

          <!-- Nice value for Syscheck process -->
          <process_priority>10</process_priority>

          <!-- Maximum output throughput -->
          <max_eps>100</max_eps>

          <!-- Database synchronization settings -->
          <synchronization>
            <enabled>yes</enabled>
            <interval>5m</interval>
            <max_interval>1h</max_interval>
            <max_eps>10</max_eps>
          </synchronization>
        </syscheck>

        <!-- Active response -->
        <global>
          <white_list>127.0.0.1</white_list>
          <white_list>^localhost.localdomain$</white_list>
        </global>

        <command>
          <name>disable-account</name>
          <executable>disable-account</executable>
          <timeout_allowed>yes</timeout_allowed>
        </command>

        <command>
          <name>restart-wazuh</name>
          <executable>restart-wazuh</executable>
        </command>

        <command>
          <name>firewall-drop</name>
          <executable>firewall-drop</executable>
          <timeout_allowed>yes</timeout_allowed>
        </command>

        <command>
          <name>host-deny</name>
          <executable>host-deny</executable>
          <timeout_allowed>yes</timeout_allowed>
        </command>

        <command>
          <name>route-null</name>
          <executable>route-null</executable>
          <timeout_allowed>yes</timeout_allowed>
        </command>

        <command>
          <name>win_route-null</name>
          <executable>route-null.exe</executable>
          <timeout_allowed>yes</timeout_allowed>
        </command>

        <command>
          <name>netsh</name>
          <executable>netsh.exe</executable>
          <timeout_allowed>yes</timeout_allowed>
        </command>

        <!--
        <active-response>
          active-response options here
        </active-response>
        -->

        <!-- Log analysis -->
        <localfile>
          <log_format>command</log_format>
          <command>df -P</command>
          <frequency>360</frequency>
        </localfile>

        <localfile>
          <log_format>full_command</log_format>
          <command>netstat -tulpn | sed 's/\([[:alnum:]]\+\)\ \+[[:digit:]]\+\ \+[[:digit:]]\+\ \+\(.*\):\([[:digit:]]*\)\ \+\([0-9\.\:\*]\+\).\+\ \([[:digit:]]*\/[[:alnum:]\-]*\).*/\1 \2 == \3 == \4 \5/' | sort -k 4 -g | sed 's/ == \(.*\) ==/:\1/' | sed 1,2d</command>
          <alias>netstat listening ports</alias>
          <frequency>360</frequency>
        </localfile>

        <localfile>
          <log_format>full_command</log_format>
          <command>last -n 20</command>
          <frequency>360</frequency>
        </localfile>

        <ruleset>
          <!-- Default ruleset -->
          <decoder_dir>ruleset/decoders</decoder_dir>
          <rule_dir>ruleset/rules</rule_dir>
          <rule_exclude>0215-policy_rules.xml</rule_exclude>
          <list>etc/lists/audit-keys</list>
          <list>etc/lists/amazon/aws-eventnames</list>
          <list>etc/lists/security-eventchannel</list>
          <list>etc/lists/malicious-ioc/malicious-ip</list>
          <list>etc/lists/malicious-ioc/malicious-domains</list>
          <list>etc/lists/malicious-ioc/malware-hashes</list>

          <!-- User-defined ruleset -->
          <decoder_dir>etc/decoders</decoder_dir>
          <rule_dir>etc/rules</rule_dir>
        </ruleset>

        <rule_test>
          <enabled>yes</enabled>
          <threads>1</threads>
          <max_sessions>64</max_sessions>
          <session_timeout>15m</session_timeout>
        </rule_test>

        <!-- Configuration for wazuh-authd -->
        <auth>
          <disabled>no</disabled>
          <port>1515</port>
          <use_source_ip>no</use_source_ip>
          <purge>yes</purge>
          <use_password>no</use_password>
          <ciphers>HIGH:!ADH:!EXP:!MD5:!RC4:!3DES:!CAMELLIA:@STRENGTH</ciphers>
          <!-- <ssl_agent_ca></ssl_agent_ca> -->
          <ssl_verify_host>no</ssl_verify_host>
          <ssl_manager_cert>etc/sslmanager.cert</ssl_manager_cert>
          <ssl_manager_key>etc/sslmanager.key</ssl_manager_key>
          <ssl_auto_negotiate>no</ssl_auto_negotiate>
        </auth>

        <cluster>
          <name>wazuh</name>
          <node_name>node01</node_name>
          <node_type>master</node_type>
          <key>aa093264ef885029653eea20dfcf51ae</key>
          <port>1516</port>
          <bind_addr>0.0.0.0</bind_addr>
          <nodes>
              <node>manager</node>
          </nodes>
          <hidden>no</hidden>
          <disabled>yes</disabled>
        </cluster>

      </ossec_config>

      <ossec_config>
        <localfile>
          <log_format>syslog</log_format>
          <location>/var/ossec/logs/active-responses.log</location>
        </localfile>

      </ossec_config>
  dashboard:
    content: |
      server.host: 0.0.0.0
      server.port: 5601
      opensearch.hosts: https://indexer:9200
      opensearch.ssl.verificationMode: certificate
      opensearch.requestHeadersWhitelist: ["securitytenant","Authorization"]
      opensearch_security.multitenancy.enabled: false
      opensearch_security.readonly_mode.roles: ["kibana_read_only"]
      # Traefik terminates HTTPS for the dashboard's domain, so the dashboard itself speaks HTTP.
      server.ssl.enabled: false
      opensearch.ssl.certificateAuthorities: ["/usr/share/wazuh-dashboard/certs/root-ca.pem"]
      uiSettings.overrides.defaultRoute: /app/wz-home
      opensearch_security.cookie.ttl: 900000
      opensearch_security.session.ttl: 900000
      opensearch_security.session.keepalive: true

volumes:
  indexer-data: {}
  indexer-snapshots: {}
  manager-api-configuration: {}
  manager-etc: {}
  manager-logs: {}
  manager-queue: {}
  manager-var-multigroups: {}
  manager-integrations: {}
  manager-active-response: {}
  manager-agentless: {}
  manager-wodles: {}
  manager-filebeat-etc: {}
  manager-filebeat-var: {}
  dashboard-config: {}
  dashboard-custom: {}
